summary: You present a coherent coral-monitoring concept, explain the value of a single spacecraft, and include STK access results. To reach the next rubric level, strengthen the evidence behind key design choices, resolve inconsistencies in orbit and communications claims, and provide a more complete, professionally presented report with reliable references.
next_steps: In Orbit and Ground Control & Communications, correct the RAAN explanation and clarify the selected orbit’s local solar time. Use the actual station geometry and access windows to support contact frequency and duration, and connect altitude and reef width to sensor field of view, ground sampling distance, and imaging performance.

In Launch and Mission Duration & EOL, verify that the launch vehicle, date, rideshare, and target orbit are feasible. Support the five-year lifetime and drag-sail disposal plan with relevant reliability, power, propellant, orbital-decay, and disposal-compliance evidence; include the software project files or reproducible design evidence.

In the Introduction, Conclusion, and Bibliography, identify the operator and clarify the operating arrangement, evaluate whether the evidence supports mission performance, and replace Wikipedia with complete, consistent, credible references. Proofread grammar and standardise figure and table labels and formatting.

criteria.C1: Your Introduction explains the coral-monitoring purpose, its public and scientific value, and why one satellite is proposed; you also name likely customers. For the next level, clearly identify the operator and operating arrangement, and strengthen the rationale and supporting references.
criteria.C2: You cover launch, orbit elements, STK access, a ground facility, mission duration, and drag-sail disposal. The STK output is useful evidence. For the next level, correct and substantiate orbit claims, validate launch feasibility, connect orbit to imaging performance, reconcile access results with communications claims, and provide software files or reproducible evidence.
criteria.C3: Your Conclusion recaps the main design choices and acknowledges launch uncertainty. To reach the next level, draw conclusions from demonstrated results: assess coverage, revisit, imaging, and data-transfer capability, and explain the effect of unresolved limitations on mission feasibility.
criteria.C4: Your report has a recognisable structure, an executive summary, labelled visuals, and a bibliography. For the next level, improve grammar and consistency in figure and table presentation, complete and standardise references, remove the disallowed Wikipedia source, and cite design claims adequately.
